plain_english: Nick's Edge Dashboard. Research screen, not a trade signal. It sums six simple checks into one score per market.
Technicals + COT + Crowd + Growth + Inflation + Jobs. 7 or more Very Bullish, 4 to 6 Bullish, -3 to 3 Neutral, -4 to -7 Bearish, -8 or less Very Bearish.

54 markets, like EdgeFinder: 29 currency pairs (the 28 majors and crosses plus USDZAR), 8 currency indexes, 8 stock indexes (with the Russell 2000), the US 10-year Treasury note (US10T), gold, silver, platinum, copper, oil, natural gas, bitcoin and ether. The added markets are scored with the same rules as the market most like them: US10T and the Russell like the other US stock indexes, platinum and copper like silver, natural gas like oil, ether like bitcoin, and USDZAR like any other pair. The added markets can be switched off in Settings.

Top Setups splits that score into 18 factors, each a whole number from -2 to +2. 1 Day Change is today's score minus the score on the trading day before. On a Saturday or Sunday it shows Friday against Thursday, the same way EdgeFinder does. The factor coverage table says which countries have a free series. A zero there means no free series, or a print with no consensus.

A score snapshot is saved for every market every day. Days before the live job started were rebuilt from saved prices, COT reports and calendar releases. Rebuilt days use the latest saved retail crowd reading, because there is no free history of it.

topic: Why a score can differ from EdgeFinder
plain_english: We use free data: Yahoo Finance prices, CFTC COT, Myfxbook or CBOE crowd readings and the Nasdaq economic calendar. EdgeFinder uses its own paid feeds. Three things cause most gaps. 1) Some releases have no forecast on the free calendar, so they score 0 here (for example Canada's manufacturing PMI and Switzerland's services PMI). 2) EdgeFinder's prices close at a different hour, so a trend that is just turning can read +1 there and +2 here. 3) Where both sides have a forecast, EdgeFinder's forecast can differ from the free one, so a single cell can flip. EURUSD shows the rules match: on Oct 24 all 14 macro cells, COT, crowd and seasonality matched EdgeFinder, and only Trend differed. CADCHF (EdgeFinder +8) differs mostly because of points 1 and 3: Canada's PMIs have no free forecast, and Canada's retail sales and jobs, and Swiss GDP and PPI, scored differently on the free calendar.
Trend score (3-day average vs 14-day average, -2 to +2) plus seasonality (+1 if this month is usually up over 10 years, -1 if usually down).
Big speculators in futures (CFTC, weekly). For a pair: did the long share rise or fall for each side. For other markets: are they net long, and did the long share rise.
Retail traders (Myfxbook). 60% or more long scores -1, 40% or less long scores +1. Indices, metals and oil use the put/call ratio instead.
Latest release beat the forecast = +1, missed = -1, for each country. For a pair the second currency is subtracted.
A high-impact event for either currency in the next 24 hours. Times are Pacific Time (PT).
COT is out Fridays for the prior Tuesday. Prices are end of day plus the latest hourly snapshot.
